narrative:
The model estimated an 87% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. In this admission process, that high estimated risk is why your law school application was denied: it treats first-time bar failure as a serious academic-risk indicator, not a certainty about your ability.

The strongest factor was your third-year class standing. Your third-year decile of 1 is far below the accepted-student average of about 5.8, and it was the top contributor pushing the prediction toward failure. The second strongest factor was your part-time status. Almost all accepted students in the comparison group planned to study full-time, while your part-time plan added further risk toward failure. The third strongest factor was your first-year class standing: a decile of 3, compared with an accepted average of 6, also pushed toward failure, though less strongly than your third-year standing. Your admission test score and undergraduate grade average are also below the accepted averages, but they were not among the three most influential factors in this decision.

To improve a future application, focus on raising your academic standing, especially in advanced coursework; consider switching to a full-time study plan or reducing work obligations; and retake the admission test after structured preparation. Seek admissions advising and document concrete improvement before reapplying.
